verses.text: My son, have you promised to pay your neighbour's debt? Have you shaken hands to guarantee a stranger's loan?
Then you are trapped by what you said. You are caught by your own words.
So do this, my son, to free yourself, because you are in your neighbour's power. Go and humble yourself. Keep begging your neighbour to let you go.
Do not let your eyes sleep. Do not even let your eyelids close.
Free yourself like a deer escaping from the hunter, like a bird escaping from the trap.
Go and look at the ant, you lazy person. Watch how it lives, and become wise.
It has no leader, no boss, and no ruler,
yet it gathers its food in summer and stores it up at harvest time.
How long will you lie there, you lazy person? When will you get up from your sleep?
A little sleep, a little rest, a little folding of the hands to rest,
and poverty will come on you like a robber, and need will attack you like an armed soldier.
A worthless and evil person goes around telling lies.
He winks with his eyes, signals with his feet, and points with his fingers.
His heart is twisted, and he is always planning evil. He is always stirring up trouble.
So disaster will come on him suddenly. In a moment he will be broken, and nothing can heal him.
There are six things the LORD hates, seven things he cannot stand:
proud eyes, a lying tongue, hands that kill innocent people,
a heart that plans evil, feet that are quick to run to do wrong,
a witness who tells lies, and a person who stirs up trouble among family members.
My son, keep your father's commands. Do not turn away from your mother's teaching.
Always keep them in your heart. Tie them around your neck.
When you walk, they will guide you. When you sleep, they will watch over you. When you wake up, they will speak to you.
These commands are a lamp, and this teaching is a light. The correction they give shows you the way to live.
They will keep you away from an immoral woman, from the smooth talk of another man's wife.
Do not long in your heart for her beauty. Do not let her catch you with her eyes.
A prostitute can be had for a loaf of bread, but another man's wife hunts for your very life.
Can a man carry fire in his lap without burning his clothes?
Can he walk on hot coals without burning his feet?
It is the same with a man who sleeps with his neighbour's wife. No one who touches her will escape punishment.
People do not hate a thief if he steals because he is starving and needs food.
But if he is caught, he must pay back seven times what he stole, even if it costs everything in his house.
But a man who commits adultery has no sense. He destroys himself.
He will be beaten and disgraced. His shame will never be wiped away.
Jealousy makes a husband furious. He will show no mercy when he takes revenge.
He will not accept any payment. He will not be satisfied, no matter how many gifts you give him.
